question.original: Find all the different viewpoints on the proper incorporation of AI-technology in an organization's strategic decision strategy.
question.restated: What distinct viewpoints does the wiki hold on how AI technology should properly be folded into an organization's strategic decision-making?
facets: Where AI sits in the strategy process (decision-support vs decision-automation; system-understanding first)
Build posture / locus of value (bolt-on vs workflow-redesign vs AI-native rebuild vs economic build/compose/use)
Human, governance & accountability factors (augmentation, learning, agents-as-employees, trust)
Where the sources genuinely disagree about the 'proper' approach

candidates.reason: Top qmd hit. The augmentation / organizational-learning viewpoint: AI as a learning substrate; explore not just exploit; explicit AI strategy correlates 2-2.6x with value (W5).
The meta-viewpoint: 10-11 frameworks operate on different decision layers; pick by the executive's question, not the framework's brand. Also names where the frameworks genuinely disagree (W1).

The strategy/system-first viewpoint: winners determined by adoption speed that helps the system, not tech access; understand feedback loops before optimizing; find-the-problem then pick the right agent level; adoption capacity is the binding constraint (W4).

The economics-first / operating-model viewpoint: USE/COMPOSE/BUILD; non-determinism as feature; embedded pods + hourglass; CFO-partnership replacing pre-flight ROI; policy-as-code governance; moats-erosion / strategic renewal (W7).
The AI-native-from-the-ground-up viewpoint: AI as operating system not tool; make the company queryable; closed-loop self-improving org; startups have the edge over incumbents (W6).
Spine concept enumerating the 10+ lenses and the cross-framework agreement (senior-leader ownership; process redesign load-bearing; models commoditize, owned assets compound) (W2).
The redesign-workflows-not-tasks viewpoint: reimagine-don't-optimize; offering/process lock-in; the named failure mode of bolt-on adoption (W3).
Distinct governance viewpoint with RCT evidence: treat agents as accountable software, not employees; anthropomorphizing diffuses accountability. Low fused_score but changes the answer (W8).
The growth-over-cost / ecosystems / trust viewpoint (China lens): aim AI at top-line business-model renewal, not cost-cutting (W9).

answer_map.claim: There is no single 'proper' way — frameworks operate on different decision layers; pick by the executive's question, not the framework's brand.
answer_map.span: Findings: The frameworks operate on different layers; Lessons

answer_map.claim: The wiki holds 10+ complementary lenses on adoption and the cross-framework agreements (senior-leader ownership; process redesign load-bearing; models commoditize while owned assets compound).
Redesign workflows, don't bolt AI onto tasks — task-level gains don't reach the P&L without reimagining the work (offering/process lock-in).
Understand the system first; winners are decided by adoption speed that helps the system, not by technology access; adoption capacity is the binding constraint; pick the right agent level.
answer_map.span: Industrial AI is in the results phase; System understanding precedes optimization; Adoption capacity is the binding constraint

answer_map.claim: Treat AI as a learning substrate — combine organizational and AI-specific learning; explore not just exploit; an explicit AI strategy correlates with 2-2.6x more value.
answer_map.span: 2x2 taxonomy; Five practical steps; Appendix strategy-value link

answer_map.claim: Build the organization AI-native from the ground up: AI as operating system not tool; closed-loop, queryable org; startups have the edge over incumbents.
answer_map.span: AI as company operating system; Open vs closed loop; Startups will win this shift

answer_map.claim: Make AI a deliberate economics-first decision (USE/COMPOSE/BUILD); treat non-determinism as a feature; embed pods + hourglass; replace pre-flight ROI with CFO-partnered opportunity-cost; govern via policy-as-code; expect moats to shift.

Govern AI as accountable software, not as employees — anthropomorphizing diffuses accountability, raises escalation, lowers error-catching; keep humans clearly accountable and don't force 1-for-1 agent roles.
answer_map.span: Four failure modes; five-point redesign prescription

answer_map.claim: Aim AI at top-line growth and business-model renewal, not cost-cutting; think ecosystems not silos; optimize for trust to scale beyond demos.
answer_map.span: The four lessons from China's no-bullshit approach

answer_map.claim: The genuine disagreements: reinvent-now vs incremental maturity; pilots-as-stage vs pilots-as-trap; org-design as prerequisite vs downstream; process-redesign-is-the-value vs the-harness-is-the-moat; and a sceptical 'most of this is rebranded systems engineering' vantage.
A productive contradiction on the destination: AI-as-employee-substitute as the end-state vs AI-as-accountable-software as the proper operating model.
